newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee market edgy, focus on Brazil weather.
newsitem.headline: German coffee market edgy, focus on Brazil weather.

text.p: Germany's physical coffee markets remain nervous as roasters look to the weather in Brazil for price direction in the next few weeks, traders said on Monday.
"There is no frost in the Brazilian growing regions for the time being, but this could change quickly," one said.
"Prices now appear to be fully based on fundamentals and they are historically high -- even without any damaging weather in Brazil," one said.
He added that the impact of the El Nino weather phenomenon on coffee crops in the west of South America, Africa and Asia was also under close scrutiny.

Traders said a recent U.S. Department of Agriculture estimate of 28 million bags for the 1997/98 Brazilian crop might be realistic because the 1996/97 crop also looked set to turn out higher than previously thought.
The USDA estimate is far above current origin and trade estimates for 1997/98, which are in a 20-25 million bags range.

But the estimate was unlikely to exert further downward pressure on prices. If it were confirmed, and if Brazil's domestic demand was deducted from the total, the data could be neutral for export supplies.
"If there was a killer frost, the anticipated 28 million bags plus carry-in from the 96/97 season would be far from good enough to satisfy global markets," a trader said.
Roasters were reasonably covered for shipments priced versus the September futures contract, importers said.
But sales offers for shipment from September were keenly awaited as roasters feared harvest delays in Central America.
Consumers were keen to swap secondary milds and steamed robustas for Centrals arabicas as soon as they became more widely available.
Arabica prices in the Bremen market were off by $8-$24 per 50 kg fob on the week, with Colombians at $226 (down $24).
But Brazils for July/August remained at $180 due to the firm domestic market and Kenyans at $370 because of tight supply.
